name: Black Walnut

facts.how: Raw or baked; strong, wine-dark flavor

caution: Husks stain hands, clothes, and driveways a permanent brown; glove up. The shells are famously hard, so think vise or hammer, not nutcracker.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Gather green balls off the ground early, before the husk blackens into dye. Stomp-roll the husks off, wash the nuts, and cure them in mesh for two weeks.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Half the people who meet black walnut love it forever; it is pecan's loud cousin, best where it can lead, in ice cream, fudge, and banana bread.
